assets.readme_context: Standalone browser tool for rotating-target geometry, LiDAR/camera architectures, angle estimation and timestamp conventions. README scope states a noise-free scene excluding range noise, classification error, boundary blur and radiometric effects; accuracy is an optimistic bound, not measured hardware performance.

assets.original_caption: Fig. 2 Hardware architecture of the proposed monitoring system, mounted inside the enclosure. The LiDAR and camera feeds are routed to the integrated processing unit via an internal Ethernet switch. The system consists of a LiDAR, camera, processing unit, and network switch, all interfaced through an IS-compliant power-and-data barrier to ensure safe operation in underground mining conditions.

assets.story_description: A colourised point cloud from a single simulated unit shows the roof canopy, face, shearer, conveyor, floor and personnel object. This is distinct from the multi-device fusion result.
assets.source_title: A Scalable Array of Integrated LiDAR–Camera Units for Continuous Colourised 3D Monitoring of Underground Longwall Operations
assets.source_version: Author-supplied local manuscript inspected 8 October 2026; figure numbering belongs to this version, not necessarily the linked public edition.
assets.caption: A colourised point cloud from a single simulated unit shows the roof canopy, face, shearer, conveyor, floor and personnel object. This is distinct from the multi-device fusion result.
assets.original_caption: Figure 17 shows the resulting colourised point cloud. The principal components of the longwall face are individually identifiable: the roof-support canopy above the device, the exposed mining face, the shearer, the conveyor, the floor, and a personnel object standing between the conveyor and the face. The output therefore provides the spatial context intended for remote assessment, allowing an operator to relate equipment positions and personnel locations to the surrounding structure rather than interpreting them from separate camera views.
assets.attribution: P. Ranasinghe, D. Patra, B. Banerjee, C. Ye, B. Nan and S. Raval. A Scalable Array of Integrated LiDAR–Camera Units for Continuous Colourised 3D Monitoring of Underground Longwall Operations. Local manuscript, Figure 17.

assets.story_description: The full pipeline links object relationships to temporal tracking, rule evaluation, contextual reasoning and a memory archive. The research diagram includes an 8 m graph edge threshold and a 10 s rolling window; these are study settings, not universal safety limits.
assets.source_title: From 3D Perception to Safety Reasoning: An Intelligent Hybrid Framework for Real-Time Underground Mine Monitoring
assets.source_version: Author-supplied local manuscript inspected 8 October 2026; figure numbering belongs to this version, not necessarily the linked public edition.
assets.caption: The full pipeline links object relationships to temporal tracking, rule evaluation, contextual reasoning and a memory archive. The research diagram includes an 8 m graph edge threshold and a 10 s rolling window; these are study settings, not universal safety limits.
assets.original_caption: Figure 7: Scene graph construction, temporal graph tracking, and memory unit generation pipeline.Nodes represent detected objects with attributes , and edges encode spatial relations within an 8 m threshold. Consecutive scene graphs are linked via inter-frame association over a 10 s rolling window to extract kinematic descriptors. Each reasoning step produces a memory unit , which is stored for longitudinal retrieval.
assets.attribution: P. Ranasinghe, S. Raval, D. Patra, B. Banerjee and I. Canbulat. From 3D Perception to Safety Reasoning: An Intelligent Hybrid Framework for Real-Time Underground Mine Monitoring. Local manuscript, Figure 7.
